chunks: Keep quiet, may Allah make you ugly, O you with broken tooth.
Certainly, by Allah, when truth became manifest even then your personality was weak and your voice was low. But when wrong began to shout loudly you again sprouted up like the horns of a kid.

key_terms.أَثْرَمُ: A title meaning 'the one with the broken tooth', referring to Amr ibn Bakr or a Kharijite leader.
key_terms.الْبَاطِلُ: Falsehood, referring to the Kharijites' deviation.
key_terms.الْحَقُّ: The Truth, referring to the rightful cause of Imam Ali.
key_terms.نُجُومَ قَرْنِ الْمَاعِزِ: The stars/horns of the young goat, a metaphor for prominent, sharp, and numerous features.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'horns of a kid' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this vivid metaphor from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) contrasts the Kharijites' initial obscurity with their sudden, noisy emergence during the decline of truth, likening their chaotic proliferation to the 'stars of the goat's horn' constellation. This imagery underscores the Shia scholarly view that their claim to piety was merely opportunistic, rising only when the established order (the truth) was challenged by internal dissent. The rebuke highlights the distinction between genuine, quiet steadfastness and the superficial, loud agitation characteristic of the Kharijite movement.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Keep quiet, may Allāh make you ugly, O you with broken tooth.
Certainly, by Allāh, when truth became manifest even then your personality was weak and your voice was lose. But when wrong began to shout loudly you again sprouted up like the horns of a kid.
